question.text: A listed company wants to buy back 6% of its paid-up capital through the open market via stock exchange after April 1, 2025. Is this permitted?

answer.text: No, open market buyback through stock exchange is not allowed from April 1, 2025
Yes, since open market buyback is always allowed for listed companies
Yes, but only if done through the book building method
Yes, if the buyback amount is less than 10% of paid-up capital

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series IX page 221, buy-back from the open market through the stock exchange is not allowed from April 1, 2025. The stem's scenario — a listed company attempting a stock-exchange-route buyback after that date — is therefore not permitted. The Trap: Open market buyback is not "always" allowed for listed companies, and the 10% paid-up-capital threshold does not unlock the prohibited stock-exchange route. Page 221 still separately lists book-building as an open-market method; the express prohibition from April 1, 2025 is targeted at the stock-exchange route specifically. Note: Limit the rule to the page 221 wording — the stock-exchange route is prohibited from April 1, 2025 — without claiming any single route is the only one permitted thereafter.
